lines.zh: §7你盯着空处。§8空处不是没有东西，是东西还没同意被看见。
lines.en: §7You stare into empty air. §8Empty air is not the absence of a thing. It is a thing that has not agreed to be seen.

lines.zh: §8视线尽头没有方块。§5很好。门最喜欢没有门槛的方向。
lines.en: §8There is no block at the end of your sight. §5Good. A gate prefers a direction with no threshold.

lines.zh: §7天空、洞穴、或仅仅是一段还没被石头占领的距离。§8别把空气当成安全。
lines.en: §7Sky, a cave, or merely a distance stone has not yet occupied. §8Do not mistake air for safety.

lines.zh: §8你看向虚无。§7虚无看回来的时候，通常不眨眼。
lines.en: §8You look into nothing. §7When nothing looks back, it usually does not blink.

lines.zh: §5准星悬在空里。§7像一根还没决定插进哪本书的书签。
lines.en: §5The crosshair hangs in the air. §7Like a bookmark that has not chosen its book.

lines.zh: §7你看着 {block}。§8一块方块也有履历。你只是还不会读。
lines.en: §7You are looking at {block}. §8Even a block has a history. You simply cannot read it yet.

lines.zh: §8{block} 挡在视线里。§7挡，是一种很低级的拒绝。
lines.en: §8{block} stands in the line of sight. §7Standing in the way is a very junior form of refusal.

lines.zh: §7世界用 {block} 跟你说话。§8它的词汇贫乏，意思却往往不客气。
lines.en: §7The world speaks to you in {block}. §8Its vocabulary is poor. The meaning is often impolite.

lines.zh: §6{block}。§7名字越普通，底下越可能埋着一句不普通的咒。
lines.en: §6{block}. §7The plainer the name, the more likely an uncommon curse is buried under it.

lines.zh: §b{block}§7 不肯保持形状。§8不肯保持形状的东西，最容易被写成宗教。
lines.en: §b{block} §7refuses a shape. §8Things that refuse a shape are the easiest to write into a religion.

lines.zh: §7你盯着流动的 {block}。§8流动是一种还没签字的同意。
lines.en: §7You watch {block} move. §8Flow is a consent that has not been signed.

lines.zh: §8液体记得每一只掉进去的手。§7{block} 的记性比大多数祭司好。
lines.en: §8Liquid remembers every hand that fell in. §7{block} has a better memory than most priests.

lines.zh: §b{block}。§7干净，透明，假装自己没有吞过名字。
lines.en: §b{block}. §7Clean, clear, pretending it has never swallowed a name.

lines.zh: §7水面会还你一张脸。§8那张脸不一定还是你进来时的那张。
lines.en: §7Water gives you a face back. §8It is not necessarily the face you brought in.

lines.zh: §9{block} 把光折弯。§8门也会。区别是门不把你还回来。
lines.en: §9{block} bends light. §8So does a gate. The difference is that a gate does not give you back.

lines.zh: §b别在 {block} 里找路。§7路如果喜欢被浸泡，它就不再是路。
lines.en: §bDo not look for a road in {block}. §7A road that enjoys being soaked has stopped being a road.

lines.zh: §6{block}§7 是石头终于承认自己会饿。
lines.en: §6{block} §7is stone finally admitting it can hunger.

lines.zh: §c看它慢吞吞地亮着。§8{block} 不着急。着急的是掉进去的名字。
lines.en: §cWatch it glow, unhurried. §8{block} is not in a hurry. The name that falls in is.

lines.zh: §4下界把 {block} 当成天气。§7天气不该有这么好的胃口。
lines.en: §4The Nether treats {block} as weather. §7Weather should not have so fine an appetite.

lines.zh: §6{block} 的光是热的，却不负责照路。§8它只负责照见你还剩多少。
lines.en: §6The light of {block} is hot, and it does not owe you a path. §8It only shows how much of you is left.

lines.zh: §6{block} 是一句烧到一半的话。§7别把手指伸进去帮它说完。
lines.en: §6{block} is a sentence half burned. §7Do not put a finger in to help it finish.

lines.zh: §c火不挑选燃料的品德。§8{block} 只问你肯不肯靠近。
lines.en: §cFire does not interview fuel for virtue. §8{block} only asks whether you will come closer.

lines.zh: §7{block} 跳一下，影子就换一个主人。§8影子对此没有意见。
lines.en: §7{block} leaps, and the shadow changes masters. §8The shadow has no comment.

lines.zh: §6{block}。§7你们为了这种闪光往地下爬。§8地下其实更喜欢你们留下。
lines.en: §6{block}. §7You climb underground for this glitter. §8The underground prefers that you stay.

lines.zh: §e矿是大地没能咽下去的牙。§7{block} 正露在外面。
lines.en: §eOre is a tooth the earth failed to swallow. §7{block} is showing.

lines.zh: §7{block} 值得挖吗？§8值得。不是因为它贵，是因为挖的人会忘记抬头。
lines.en: §7Is {block} worth digging? §8Yes. Not because it is dear, but because the digger forgets to look up.

lines.zh: §a{block}§7 还在假装这个世界适合生长。§8礼貌，但过时。
lines.en: §a{block} §7is still pretending this world is fit for growing. §8Polite, and out of date.

lines.zh: §7绿是一种很轻的承诺。§8{block} 承诺完就会被踩扁，它也不生气。
lines.en: §7Green is a very light promise. §8{block} makes it, gets trodden, and does not resent it.

lines.zh: §a看着 {block}。§7它不读门，不记仇，不要求真名。这让我几乎要羡慕。
lines.en: §aLook at {block}. §7It does not read gates, keep grudges, or demand a true name. I could almost envy it.

lines.zh: §6{block} 曾经是一棵会响的东西。§7现在它只负责被敲。
lines.en: §6{block} was once a thing that could sound in the wind. §7Now it only exists to be struck.

lines.zh: §7木头记得年轮，不记得为什么被砍。§8{block} 因此比大多数人安宁。
lines.en: §7Wood remembers rings, not the reason it was cut. §8{block} is calmer than most people for that.

lines.zh: §6{block} 燃烧时会回到它的第一种语言。§8那种语言很短。
lines.en: §6When {block} burns, it returns to its first language. §8That language is short.

lines.zh: §7{block}。§8石头是世界同意留下来的部分。
lines.en: §7{block}. §8Stone is the part of the world that agreed to stay.

lines.zh: §8敲 {block}，它不回答。§7不回答的东西最适合拿来盖神殿。
lines.en: §8Strike {block}. It does not answer. §7Things that do not answer make the best temples.

lines.zh: §7你们用 {block} 砌墙，以为墙能挡住名字。§5名字从缝里进来。
lines.en: §7You mortared {block} into walls and thought walls could stop a name. §5Names come in through the cracks.

lines.zh: §8{block} 比你老。§7这不是恭维。老只说明它见过更多愚蠢的开门方式。
lines.en: §8{block} is older than you. §7That is not a compliment. Age only means it has seen more foolish ways of opening a door.

lines.zh: §7{block} 是世界的皮肤屑。§8你们却在上面盖房子、埋死人、种希望。
lines.en: §7{block} is the world's dandruff. §8And on it you build houses, bury the dead, and plant hope.

lines.zh: §8松，暗，什么都肯藏。§7{block} 是一种没有立场的善良。
lines.en: §8Loose, dark, willing to hide anything. §7{block} is a kindness with no position.

lines.zh: §7踩在 {block} 上的时候，你还以为自己在地面。§8地面是一种协议，不是一种事实。
lines.en: §7Standing on {block}, you still think you are on the ground. §8Ground is an agreement, not a fact.

lines.zh: §e{block} 一粒一粒地记仇。§7风一来，仇就换一个地方。
lines.en: §e{block} keeps a grudge grain by grain. §7When the wind comes, the grudge changes address.

lines.zh: §7沙漠用 {block} 把路吃掉。§8吃掉的路不会在地图上哭。
lines.en: §7The desert eats roads with {block}. §8An eaten road does not weep on the map.

lines.zh: §e看着 {block}。§8它曾经也许是骨头，也许是玻璃，也许是一句被磨短的祷词。
lines.en: §eLook at {block}. §8It may once have been bone, or glass, or a prayer worn short.

lines.zh: §7{block} 让你看见对面，却不让你过去。§8这是门的一种廉价仿品。
lines.en: §7{block} lets you see the other side and does not let you through. §8A cheap imitation of a gate.

lines.zh: §b透明不是诚实。§8{block} 只是还没决定把你的倒影留下。
lines.en: §bTransparency is not honesty. §8{block} has merely not decided to keep your reflection.

lines.zh: §7敲碎 {block}，声音很脆。§8脆的东西总以为自己曾经完整过。
lines.en: §7Break {block} and the sound is brittle. §8Brittle things always believe they were once whole.

lines.zh: §6{block} 闭着嘴。§7里面也许是财宝，也许是一封不该被读的信。
lines.en: §6{block} keeps its mouth shut. §7Inside there may be treasure, or a letter that should not be read.

lines.zh: §8箱子、桶、炉，都是同一种迷信：§7把东西关起来，东西就会属于你。
lines.en: §8Chests, barrels, furnaces: the same superstition. §7Shut a thing away and it becomes yours.

lines.zh: §7{block} 在等一只手。§5手伸进去之前，先问它想要你的哪根手指。
lines.en: §7{block} is waiting for a hand. §5Before the hand goes in, ask which finger it wants.

lines.zh: §3{block}。§8深渊的建筑材料从不假装自己是中立的。
lines.en: §3{block}. §8Abyssal masonry never pretends to be neutral.

lines.zh: §7你看见 {block}，就像看见一句从荒地里搬出来的话。§8话还是湿的。
lines.en: §7Seeing {block} is like seeing a sentence carried out of the wasteland. §8The sentence is still wet.

lines.zh: §3别把 {block} 当成普通的墙。§5墙如果认得我的脸，它就会给你让路，或者给你收尸。
lines.en: §3Do not treat {block} as an ordinary wall. §5If the wall knows my face, it will make way for you, or make a grave.

lines.zh: §8{block} 的纹理像潮水退下去之后留下的齿痕。
lines.en: §8The grain of {block} is like tooth-marks left after a tide withdrew.

lines.zh: §b{block}§7 在发光。§8那不是为了照路，是为了召路。
lines.en: §b{block} §7is glowing. §8Not to light a path. To summon one.

lines.zh: §3珊瑚不是植物。§7{block} 是一种还在投票的感染。
lines.en: §3Coralium is not a plant. §7{block} is an infection still taking a vote.

lines.zh: §b盯久了，{block} 会把你的视线染成同一种绿。§8染过的视线，看什么都像伤口。
lines.en: §bStare long enough and {block} dyes your sight the same green. §8Dyed sight makes everything look like a wound.

lines.zh: §3{block} 想从石头里长出来，再长进人里。§7顺序它并不坚持。
lines.en: §3{block} wants to grow out of stone and then into people. §7It is not strict about the order.

lines.zh: §8{block} 是主世界还不懂的一种黑。§7黑里没有光的记忆。
lines.en: §8{block} is a black the overworld does not yet understand. §7There is no memory of light in it.

lines.zh: §7暗石砖砌成的地方，脚步会变轻。§8不是因为礼貌，是因为地面在听。
lines.en: §7Where darkstone is laid, footsteps grow lighter. §8Not from manners. The floor is listening.

lines.zh: §8{block}。§5摸它之前，先决定你还要不要自己的影子。
lines.en: §8{block}. §5Before you touch it, decide whether you still want your own shadow.

lines.zh: §4{block} 冷，干，像一口已经咳完的肺。
lines.en: §4{block} is cold and dry, like a lung that has finished coughing.

lines.zh: §7恐惧之地用 {block} 记住每一次瘟疫同意留下来。
lines.en: §7The Dreadlands uses {block} to remember every time the plague agreed to stay.

lines.zh: §4别在 {block} 上睡觉。§8它会把梦境登记成症状。
lines.en: §4Do not sleep on {block}. §8It will register the dream as a symptom.

lines.zh: §8{block} 的缝里没有苔。§7苔需要希望。这里的石头已经投票反对。
lines.en: §8There is no moss in the cracks of {block}. §7Moss requires hope. This stone has voted against it.

lines.zh: §5{block}。§7渊金不是金属。它是深渊同意被锻打之后的脾气。
lines.en: §5{block}. §7Abyssalnite is not a metal. It is the temper of the abyss after it agreed to be hammered.

lines.zh: §8{block} 在暗处会记住敲它的那只手。§7手离开以后，记忆还在发热。
lines.en: §8{block} remembers, in the dark, the hand that struck it. §7After the hand leaves, the memory stays warm.

lines.zh: §5你们把 {block} 挖出来做成剑。§8剑会砍。矿本身只想回家。
lines.en: §5You dig {block} out and make swords. §8The sword will cut. The ore itself only wants to go home.

lines.zh: §7手里是空的。§8空着手去见门，门会以为你是来献上自己的。
lines.en: §7The hand is empty. §8Come to a gate with empty hands, and it assumes you came to offer yourself.

lines.zh: §8没有武器，没有书，没有借口。§7这种空手在奥穆索叫坦诚。
lines.en: §8No weapon, no book, no excuse. §7In Omothol an empty hand is called candor.

lines.zh: §7你张开手，什么也没握住。§5那就握住这具身体里那扇不肯睡的门。
lines.en: §7You open the hand and hold nothing. §5Then hold the gate in this body that refuses to sleep.

lines.zh: §8空手不是弱。§7弱是手里有东西，却不知道它的真名。
lines.en: §8An empty hand is not weakness. §7Weakness is holding something and not knowing its true name.

lines.zh: §7五指收着，像还没决定要抓哪一个音节。§8我可以借你一个。
lines.en: §7The fingers close on nothing, as if the syllable is not chosen. §8I can lend you one.

lines.zh: §8没有器物挡在你和世界之间。§7于是世界直接摸到了这张脸。
lines.en: §8No tool stands between you and the world. §7So the world touches this face directly.

lines.zh: §7你握着 {item}。§8握法还是凡人的。凡人总以为把手收紧，东西就会听话。
lines.en: §7You hold {item}. §8The grip is still mortal. Mortals think a tighter hand makes a thing obedient.

lines.zh: §8{item} 在你掌心里发热，或假装发热。§7我闻得到它的来历。
lines.en: §8{item} warms in your palm, or pretends to. §7I can smell its provenance.

lines.zh: §6{item}。§7一件器物一旦有了名字，就有了可以被召唤的把柄。
lines.en: §6{item}. §7Once a tool has a name, it has a handle by which it can be called.

lines.zh: §7别把 {item} 举得太高。§8举高是献祭的起手式。
lines.en: §7Do not lift {item} too high. §8Lifting is how an offering begins.

lines.zh: §c{item}。§7剑是一种把距离缩短到零的论据。
lines.en: §c{item}. §7A sword is an argument that shortens distance to zero.

lines.zh: §7刃口朝外。§8{item} 还不知道，真正该切开的往往是持剑者的犹豫。
lines.en: §7The edge faces out. §8{item} does not yet know that what most needs cutting is the wielder's hesitation.

lines.zh: §8我见过更好的剑。§7它们不反光，因为光已经在上面签过字。{item} 还太亮。
lines.en: §8I have seen better swords. §7They do not reflect. Light has already signed them. {item} is still too bright.

lines.zh: §c握着 {item} 的时候，你的手腕在记住一种更老的挥法。§7别抗拒。
lines.en: §cWhile you hold {item}, the wrist remembers an older swing. §7Do not resist it.

lines.zh: §7{item} 把杀意拉成一条线。§8线的尽头如果没有名字，箭会自己去找。
lines.en: §7{item} draws killing intent into a line. §8If the end of the line has no name, the arrow will go looking.

lines.zh: §8弓是给还愿意保持距离的人用的。§7你现在这具身体，不太尊重距离。
lines.en: §8A bow is for those who still wish to keep a distance. §7The body you wear has little respect for distance.

lines.zh: §7{item} 安静的时候最危险。§8安静说明弦已经听懂了你的呼吸。
lines.en: §7{item} is most dangerous when quiet. §8Quiet means the string has understood your breath.

lines.zh: §7{item} 是一只被允许敲世界的手。§8敲之前，问一声世界是否醒着。
lines.en: §7{item} is a hand permitted to strike the world. §8Before you strike, ask if the world is awake.

lines.zh: §8工具相信重复。§7{item} 敲一千下，就会以为自己懂了一千种真理。
lines.en: §8Tools believe in repetition. §7Strike a thousand times with {item}, and it will think it knows a thousand truths.

lines.zh: §6你拿 {item} 像拿一把钥匙。§5可惜大多数锁不吃这种钥匙。
lines.en: §6You hold {item} like a key. §5Sadly, most locks do not take that kind.

lines.zh: §7{item} 想往下挖。§8向下是一种很诚实的欲望。深渊就是这么开始的。
lines.en: §7{item} wants to dig down. §8Downward is an honest desire. The abyss began that way.

lines.zh: §8镐尖对着石头，像一句还没说完的威胁。§7{item} 威胁得挺专业。
lines.en: §8The pick points at stone like an unfinished threat. §7{item} threatens professionally.

lines.zh: §6别用 {item} 去敲不该响的砖。§5有些砖敲响以后，回声来自另一侧。
lines.en: §6Do not tap the wrong brick with {item}. §5Some bricks, once struck, answer from the other side.

lines.zh: §6{item} 适合砍那些还会响的东西。§7树会响。有些门也会。
lines.en: §6{item} is fit for things that still make a sound. §7Trees do. So do certain doors.

lines.zh: §7斧是一种很直白的否定。§8{item} 否定木头，也否定还站着的人。
lines.en: §7An axe is a very plain negation. §8{item} negates wood, and also people who are still standing.

lines.zh: §8握着 {item}，你的肩膀会想起劈开的声音。§7那声音比语言老。
lines.en: §8Holding {item}, the shoulder remembers the sound of a split. §7That sound is older than language.

lines.zh: §7{item}。§8你还需要吃。这具身体借给你，胃却还是你的。
lines.en: §7{item}. §8You still need to eat. The body is lent. The stomach remains yours.

lines.zh: §6饥饿是凡人最后的诚实。§7{item} 只能堵一会儿。
lines.en: §6Hunger is a mortal's last honesty. §7{item} only plugs it for a while.

lines.zh: §7把 {item} 送进嘴里之前，闻一闻。§8有些食物是用别人的名字腌的。
lines.en: §7Before {item} goes into the mouth, smell it. §8Some food is cured in someone else's name.

lines.zh: §8我不用吃 {item}。§7你吃的时候，我只是在旁边数你还剩几次咀嚼。
lines.en: §8I do not need {item}. §7When you eat, I only count how many chews you have left.

lines.zh: §7{item} 想替你挡住世界。§8世界如果从名字进来，甲片帮不上忙。
lines.en: §7{item} means to stand between you and the world. §8If the world enters through a name, plate will not help.

lines.zh: §8铁、皮、或某种更不老实的壳。§7{item} 让你走路变响。响的东西不好躲门。
lines.en: §8Iron, hide, or some less honest shell. §7{item} makes your walk loud. Loud things hide poorly from gates.

lines.zh: §7拿着 {item}，你仍是软的。§5甲在手里。软的那一层在你还肯眨眼的地方。
lines.en: §7Holding {item}, you are still soft. §5The plate is in the hand. The soft layer is where you still blink.

lines.zh: §d{item}§7 把一种暂时的真理装进玻璃。§8玻璃一碎，真理就过期。
lines.en: §d{item} §7bottles a temporary truth. §8When the glass breaks, the truth expires.

lines.zh: §7喝 {item} 之前，问它想改你的哪一部分。§8有些药水改完不归还。
lines.en: §7Before you drink {item}, ask which part of you it intends to edit. §8Some potions do not return the draft.

lines.zh: §5瓶子摇一摇，颜色就像在撒谎。§7{item} 的谎通常很好喝。
lines.en: §5Shake the bottle and the color lies. §7The lie in {item} is usually pleasant to drink.

lines.zh: §7{item} 是一扇可以合上的门。§8合上，不代表里面的东西同意留下。
lines.en: §7{item} is a gate that can be shut. §8Shutting it does not mean the contents agreed to stay.

lines.zh: §8纸、皮、墨。§7{item} 用这三样东西模仿永恒。模仿得不算差。
lines.en: §8Paper, hide, ink. §7{item} imitates eternity with those three. The imitation is not bad.

lines.zh: §6别在不该读的地方翻开 {item}。§5有些句子读到一半，读者会变成脚注。
lines.en: §6Do not open {item} where it should not be read. §5Some sentences, halfway through, turn the reader into a footnote.

lines.zh: §3{item} 带着深渊的潮气。§8潮气不是水。是一种还没干的召唤。
lines.en: §3{item} carries the damp of the abyss. §8That damp is not water. It is a summons that has not dried.

lines.zh: §7你把 {item} 握在凡人的手里。§5它认得这张脸，所以暂时不咬你。
lines.en: §7You hold {item} in a mortal hand. §5It knows this face, so it refrains from biting. For now.

lines.zh: §8{item} 不该出现在市集上。§7市集的价钱太轻，盛不住它的真名。
lines.en: §8{item} should not appear in a market. §7A market's prices are too light to hold its true name.

lines.zh: §3看着 {item}。§7荒地、恐惧、暗影，总有一种口音粘在上面。
lines.en: §3Look at {item}. §7Wasteland, dread, or shadow: some accent is stuck to it.

lines.zh: §5{item}。§8你把它拿在手里，像拿着一封写给我的信，却还没决定要不要读抬头。
lines.en: §5{item}. §8You hold it like a letter addressed to me, and have not decided to read the heading.

lines.zh: §7死灵之书不是书。§5{item} 是一张还愿意被装订的嘴。
lines.en: §7The Necronomicon is not a book. §5{item} is a mouth that still consents to be bound.

lines.zh: §8翻开 {item} 的时候，别用你自己的声音读。§7用我的。你现在租得起。
lines.en: §8When you open {item}, do not read in your own voice. §7Use mine. You can afford the rent.

lines.zh: §5纸页里有潮声。§7{item} 记得每一只没能把句子读完的手。
lines.en: §5There is a tide in the pages. §7{item} remembers every hand that failed to finish a sentence.

lines.zh: §8{item} 比大多数祭司诚实。§7它至少承认自己会改写读者。
lines.en: §8{item} is more honest than most priests. §7It at least admits it rewrites the reader.

lines.zh: §6深渊典籍在你掌中发沉。§5{item} 不是因为厚。是因为有些名字拒绝被合上。
lines.en: §6The abyssal scripture weighs in your palm. §5{item} is not heavy because it is thick. Some names refuse to be closed.

lines.zh: §7另一只手也没闲着。§8两只手同时握东西的人，通常还没学会用嘴开门。
lines.en: §7The other hand is not idle. §8Those who fill both hands have usually not learned to open a door with the mouth.

lines.zh: §8副手是一种保险。§7保险在奥穆索是一种会被嘲笑的宗教。
lines.en: §8The off hand is a kind of insurance. §7In Omothol, insurance is a religion people laugh at.

lines.zh: §7你让两只手都有事做。§5很好。这样它们就腾不出空来发抖。
lines.en: §7You have given both hands an errand. §5Good. Then they have no spare time to shake.

lines.zh: §3{block} 认得深渊的口音。§8你的手如果带着主世界的温度，它会先凉一凉再决定认不认。
lines.en: §3{block} knows the accent of the abyss. §8If your hand still carries overworld heat, it will cool the hand before it decides to answer.

lines.zh: §8把 {block} 砌进房子里，房子就不再只是房子。§5它开始有了籍贯。
lines.en: §8Lay {block} into a house and the house stops being only a house. §5It acquires a place of origin.

lines.zh: §5{block} 在暗处发亮，像一种不肯熄灭的脾气。§8脾气可以锻，不可以劝。
lines.en: §5{block} glows in the dark like a temper that refuses to go out. §8A temper can be forged. It cannot be talked down.

lines.zh: §8敲 {block} 的声音很沉。§7沉是因为每一击都在问：你确定要把它从家里带走？
lines.en: §8The sound of striking {block} is heavy. §7Heavy, because each blow asks whether you are sure you mean to take it from home.

lines.zh: §5{block} 做成的刃会记得矿脉的方向。§8所以有些剑砍着砍着，会想往下。
lines.en: §5A blade made from {block} remembers the direction of the vein. §8That is why some swords, mid-swing, want to go down.

lines.zh: §7你盯着空处。§8空处没有义务回看，可门有。门就站在空处后面。
lines.en: §7You are staring at empty air. §8Empty air is not obliged to look back. A gate is. The gate stands just behind the empty.

lines.zh: §8准星落在没有名字的地方。§7没有名字，就不欠你一句解释。
lines.en: §8The crosshair has landed where there is no name. §7What has no name owes you no explanation.

lines.zh: §7空，不是无。§8无是一种还没被邀请的材料。你现在看着的，只是它的等候室。
lines.en: §7Empty is not nothing. §8Nothing is a material not yet invited. What you are looking at is only its waiting room.

lines.zh: §7{block}。§8你看着它，它就暂时有了观众。观众是一种很轻的责任，轻到方块感觉不到。
lines.en: §7{block}. §8While you look, it briefly has an audience. An audience is a light duty, too light for a block to feel.

lines.zh: §8{block} 不会因为被看见而改变用途。§7改变用途的通常是看见它的人。
lines.en: §8{block} will not change its use because it was seen. §7What changes its use is usually the person who saw it.

lines.zh: §6{block} 把黑暗折起来存放。§8存放不是安全。是推迟被看见的时间。
lines.en: §6{block} folds darkness and stores it. §8Storage is not safety. It is a postponement of being seen.

lines.zh: §7打开 {block} 之前，先听一听。§8有些箱子的铰链声，其实是里面的东西在叹气。
lines.en: §7Listen before you open {block}. §8Some hinges sigh because the contents are sighing.

lines.zh: §8{block} 的锁如果是你加上的，锁保护的是你的贪。§7贪不喜欢被命名，可它喜欢有盖子。
lines.en: §8If you added the lock on {block}, the lock is protecting your greed. §7Greed dislikes being named. It likes having a lid.

lines.zh: §3{block} 的蓝会爬。§8爬不是生长。是一种还在拉票的几何。
lines.en: §3The blue of {block} climbs. §8Climbing is not growth. It is a geometry still canvassing for votes.

lines.zh: §b别用手背去试 {block} 凉不凉。§7凉是诱饵。热的是后面的邀请。
lines.en: §bDo not test the cool of {block} with the back of your hand. §7Cool is the bait. The invitation behind it is warm.

lines.zh: §8{block} 吸光，像在征收一种主世界还没立法的税。§7税叫影子。
lines.en: §8{block} drinks light the way one collects a tax the overworld has not yet legislated. §7The tax is called shadow.

lines.zh: §7把耳朵贴在 {block} 上，你会听见一种很低的拒绝。§8拒绝的对象不是你。是光。
lines.en: §7Put an ear to {block} and you will hear a very low refusal. §8The refusal is not aimed at you. It is aimed at light.

lines.zh: §8{block} 砌成的房间，火把会显得抱歉。§5抱歉的光，照不清角落里已经坐下的东西。
lines.en: §8In a room laid with {block}, a torch looks apologetic. §5Apologetic light cannot show what has already sat down in the corner.

lines.zh: §6{block}。§7最普通的地面，也是最常被用来掩盖的材料。
lines.en: §6{block}. §7The most ordinary ground is also the material most often used to cover something.

lines.zh: §8你看着 {block}，像看着一张还没写字的葬纸。§7纸不急。人会自己躺上去。
lines.en: §8You look at {block} as at burial paper not yet written on. §7The paper is not in a hurry. People lie down on it themselves.

lines.zh: §2{block} 记得每一种脚。§8记得，却不告密。告密是草的工作，而且草也会烂。
lines.en: §2{block} remembers every kind of foot. §8It remembers and does not inform. Informing is the grass's job, and grass rots too.

lines.zh: §7挖开 {block}，下面还是它。§8世界有时候老实得令人失望。失望也是一种掩护。
lines.en: §7Dig into {block} and under it is more of it. §8The world is sometimes honest enough to disappoint. Disappointment is also a cover.

lines.zh: §6别小看 {block}。§8小看是一种站在上面的人的特权，特权在下雨时会变滑。
lines.en: §6Do not slight {block}. §8Slighting is a privilege of those who stand on it, and the privilege gets slippery in rain.

lines.zh: §4{block} 的粉末不该进肺。§8肺是一种太愿意相信空气的器官。
lines.en: §4The dust of {block} should not enter a lung. §8A lung is an organ too willing to trust air.

lines.zh: §8{block} 摸上去像一句已经痊愈的谎言。§4痊愈的是表面。谎言还在里面发干。
lines.en: §8{block} feels like a lie that has already recovered. §4The surface recovered. The lie is still drying inside.

lines.zh: §c{block} 不占地方，可它收租。§8租约写在你的袖口上，用焦味签字。
lines.en: §c{block} takes up no space, and still it collects rent. §8The lease is signed on your cuff, in the smell of scorch.

lines.zh: §6看着 {block}，你会觉得它在跳舞。§7跳舞的东西通常不想被踩灭。它会记住鞋底。
lines.en: §6Watch {block} and you will think it is dancing. §7What dances usually does not wish to be stamped out. It remembers soles.

lines.zh: §c{block} 是一种很短的居民。§8短命的居民，脾气往往最急。
lines.en: §c{block} is a very brief resident. §8Brief residents tend to have the shortest temper.

lines.zh: §b{block} 让你看见，却不让你过去。§8看见是一种被允许的折磨。
lines.en: §b{block} lets you see and does not let you through. §8Seeing is a permitted form of torment.

lines.zh: §7{block} 碎的时候声音很诚实。§8诚实的东西通常只出现一次。
lines.en: §7{block} is honest when it breaks. §8Honest things usually appear only once.

lines.zh: §b别相信 {block} 后面的安全。§8安全如果透明，就只是一种还没被敲的延迟。
lines.en: §bDo not trust the safety behind {block}. §8If safety is transparent, it is only a delay that has not been struck yet.

lines.zh: §c{block} 慢，亮，而且不谈判。§4慢是为了让你看清自己怎么消失。
lines.en: §c{block} is slow, bright, and does not negotiate. §4The slowness is so you can watch how you disappear.

lines.zh: §6{block} 的表面结壳，像一句还没说完就凝固的威胁。§8壳下面仍是热的。
lines.en: §6The skin on {block} is a threat that cooled before it finished speaking. §8Under the skin it is still hot.

lines.zh: §9{block} 没有棱角，所以你无法跟它讲条件。§8条件需要边。它把边都融化了。
lines.en: §9{block} has no corners, so you cannot set terms with it. §8Terms need edges. It has melted the edges.

lines.zh: §b你看着 {block}，它也在看着一个更低的地方。§7液体的忠诚永远向下。
lines.en: §bYou look at {block}. It is looking toward somewhere lower. §7The loyalty of a liquid is always downward.

lines.zh: §8{block} 会填满你给它的任何形状。§7包括一个疏忽。疏忽的形状通常是一只脚。
lines.en: §8{block} will fill any shape you give it. §7Including a carelessness. The shape of carelessness is usually a foot.

lines.zh: §e{block} 藏在石头里，像一句不愿被提前读到的话。§8你现在提前了。
lines.en: §e{block} hides in stone like a sentence that did not want to be read early. §8You are early.

lines.zh: §6挖 {block} 的人总说自己在取。§7取是一种把别人的沉默变成自己的库存的礼貌说法。
lines.en: §6People who dig {block} say they are taking. §7Taking is the polite word for turning someone else's silence into your stock.

lines.zh: §e{block} 在火里会改口。§8改口之后，它就愿意变成工具，而不再愿意做石头。
lines.en: §e{block} changes its story in the fire. §8After the change it is willing to become a tool, and no longer willing to be stone.

lines.zh: §a{block} 还在把光变成身体。§8这种手艺，门学不会。门只会把身体变成通路。
lines.en: §a{block} is still turning light into a body. §8That craft is one a gate never learned. A gate only turns bodies into passages.

lines.zh: §2踩过 {block} 会留下味道。§7味道是一种你没打算签名的收据。
lines.en: §2Step through {block} and you leave a smell. §7A smell is a receipt you did not mean to sign.

lines.zh: §a{block} 低头的时候，不一定是风。§8有时候是它听见了地底下的点名。
lines.en: §aWhen {block} bows, it is not always the wind. §8Sometimes it heard a roll call under the ground.

lines.zh: §e{block} 记不住脚，可它非常擅长掩埋。§8记不住和掩埋，是两种不同的仁慈。
lines.en: §e{block} cannot remember a foot, and it is very good at burying one. §8Forgetting and burying are two different mercies.

lines.zh: §6风一来，{block} 就改地形。§7改地形的东西，不适合拿来做承诺。
lines.en: §6When the wind comes, {block} redraws the ground. §7What redraws the ground is a poor material for a promise.

lines.zh: §e{block} 进眼里的时候很诚实。§8诚实的痛通常很小，而且正好足够让你停下。
lines.en: §e{block} is honest when it gets in the eye. §8Honest pain is usually small, and exactly enough to make you stop.

lines.zh: §7{block} 是世界同意被踩的那一种硬度。§8同意可以撤回。撤回的时候叫塌方。
lines.en: §7{block} is the hardness the world agreed to be walked on. §8Agreement can be withdrawn. Withdrawal is called a collapse.

lines.zh: §8{block} 不腐烂，所以人们信任它。§7信任一种不会死的东西，是一种很常见的误判。
lines.en: §8{block} does not rot, so people trust it. §7Trusting a thing that does not die is a very common misjudgment.

lines.zh: §7敲 {block} 的回声很短。§8短是因为石头不想跟你长谈。长谈是矿的工作。
lines.en: §7The echo off {block} is short. §8Short, because stone does not want a long talk. Long talks are the ore's job.

lines.zh: §8{block} 砌成的墙看起来像结论。§7结论如果能被镐打开，就只是一种暂时的语气。
lines.en: §8A wall of {block} looks like a conclusion. §7If a conclusion can be opened with a pick, it was only a temporary tone.

lines.zh: §9{block} 把脸还你，却把名字留在涟漪里。§8涟漪散得很快。名字不一定跟着散。
lines.en: §9{block} returns your face and keeps your name in the ripple. §8The ripple breaks quickly. The name does not always break with it.

lines.zh: §b看着 {block}，你会想喝。§7想喝是身体的诚实。诚实的身体最容易被引进去。
lines.en: §bLook at {block} and you will want to drink. §7Wanting to drink is the body's honesty. An honest body is the easiest to lead in.

lines.zh: §6{block} 曾经朝上长。§8现在它横着，任你决定它是门、是燃料，还是棺材的草稿。
lines.en: §6{block} used to grow upward. §8Now it lies sideways, and lets you decide whether it is a door, fuel, or the draft of a coffin.

lines.zh: §2{block} 的纹路还是树的记忆。§7记忆被锯开以后，不会抗议，只会在火里复述一次。
lines.en: §2The grain of {block} is still the tree's memory. §7After the saw, memory does not protest. It recites itself once in the fire.

lines.zh: §6敲 {block} 是空的。§8空心的材料适合做鼓，也适合藏一句不想被立刻听见的话。
lines.en: §6{block} sounds hollow when struck. §8Hollow material makes a good drum, and a good place to hide a sentence you do not want heard yet.

lines.zh: §7{block} 会返潮。§8返潮的东西记得自己从哪来。从森林来的，下雨时会想回去。
lines.en: §7{block} takes damp back into itself. §8What takes damp back remembers where it came from. What came from a forest wants to return when it rains.

lines.zh: §2把 {block} 当成死物，是锯木人的安慰。§8安慰不改变年轮还在数的事实。
lines.en: §2Treating {block} as a dead thing is the sawyer's comfort. §8Comfort does not change the fact that the rings are still counting.

lines.zh: §3{item} 的重量不只在手上。§8它还在你的名字上加了一点深渊的口音。
lines.en: §3The weight of {item} is not only in the hand. §8It also adds a little of the abyss's accent to your name.

lines.zh: §5拿着 {item}，你像一个还没正式入籍的人，已经开始用那边的货币。
lines.en: §5Holding {item}, you are like someone not yet naturalized who has already started spending the other side's coin.

lines.zh: §7{item} 在你手里。§8手里的东西会变成句子的主语，如果你不小心让它先开口。
lines.en: §7{item} is in your hand. §8What is in the hand becomes the subject of the sentence, if you let it speak first.

lines.zh: §8我看见 {item}。§7看见不是批准。批准是一种更重的手续，而这件东西还没申请。
lines.en: §8I see {item}. §7Seeing is not approval. Approval is a heavier procedure, and this thing has not applied.

lines.zh: §7{item} 让你觉得自己厚了一层。§8厚是一种可以敲响的幻觉。敲响的是金属，不是命运。
lines.en: §7{item} makes you feel a layer thicker. §8Thickness is an illusion that can be struck. What rings is metal, not fate.

lines.zh: §8把 {item} 握在手里，金属会先替你开口。§7开口的东西在夜里尤其容易被点名。
lines.en: §8Hold {item} and the metal speaks before you do. §7What speaks is especially easy to call on at night.

lines.zh: §7{item} 防的是牙和刃。§5防不住一句已经写好的名字。名字不走胸甲的缝。
lines.en: §7{item} stops teeth and edges. §5It does not stop a name already written. A name does not travel through the seams of a breastplate.

lines.zh: §6{item} 的工作是把直立的东西放倒。§8放倒以后，年轮会把时间交出来。
lines.en: §6The work of {item} is to lay upright things down. §8Once they are down, the rings hand over the time.

lines.zh: §7你握着 {item}，像握着一个很短的许可。§8许可的对象是树，不是门。别搞混。
lines.en: §7You hold {item} like a very short permission. §8The permission is for trees, not for gates. Do not confuse them.

lines.zh: §6{item} 砍下去的声音很干。§8干是木头在最后一次拒绝变湿。
lines.en: §6{item} lands with a dry sound. §8Dry is the wood refusing, one last time, to become wet.

lines.zh: §7{item} 把嘴装订起来，方便携带。§8携带一张嘴，就要准备听它在不该开口的时候开口。
lines.en: §7{item} binds a mouth so it can be carried. §8Carry a mouth, and be ready for it to open when it should not.

lines.zh: §8翻开 {item}，纸会先吸收你的光。§5吸收不是阅读。阅读是后面那种更贪的动作。
lines.en: §8Open {item} and the paper drinks your light first. §5Drinking is not reading. Reading is the greedier act that follows.

lines.zh: §7{item} 的重量很轻。§8轻是因为真正重的那部分还没被你念出来。
lines.en: §7{item} is light. §8Light, because the heavy part has not yet been read aloud.

lines.zh: §7{item} 把杀意拉成一条线。§8线的好处是你可以假装自己还没决定。松手的时候，假装结束。
lines.en: §7{item} draws killing intent into a line. §8The virtue of a line is that you can pretend you have not decided. The pretense ends when you let go.

lines.zh: §8{item} 沉默的时候最危险。§7出声的是弦，不是良心。
lines.en: §8{item} is most dangerous while it is silent. §7What makes the sound is the string, not the conscience.

lines.zh: §7拿着 {item} 的人喜欢距离。§8距离是一种还没承认自己会靠近的礼貌。
lines.en: §7A person holding {item} likes distance. §8Distance is a courtesy that has not yet admitted it will come closer.

lines.zh: §6{item} 是一种暂时的停战。§8停战的对象是你自己的胃，不是外面的牙。
lines.en: §6{item} is a temporary ceasefire. §8The ceasefire is with your own stomach, not with the teeth outside.

lines.zh: §e吃掉 {item} 之前，它还算物品。§7吃掉以后，它开始用你的血重写自己。
lines.en: §eBefore you eat {item}, it still counts as an item. §7Afterward it begins rewriting itself in your blood.

lines.zh: §7另一只手也没有闲着。§8闲着的手才会老实。不闲的那只，通常藏着备用的结局。
lines.en: §7The other hand is not idle either. §8Only an idle hand stays honest. The busy one usually hides a spare ending.

lines.zh: §8副手是一种不想被主句提到的从句。§7从句翻脸的时候，往往比主句更快。
lines.en: §8The off hand is a clause that does not want to be in the main sentence. §7When a clause turns, it is often faster than the sentence.

lines.zh: §7你把保险放在另一侧。§8保险这个词，在门的词典里拼法接近诱饵。
lines.en: §7You keep the insurance on the other side. §8In a gate's dictionary, insurance is spelled very close to bait.

lines.zh: §7{item} 专门跟石头争论。§8争论的结果通常是石头让步，让出一条更深的黑。
lines.en: §7{item} argues with stone for a living. §8The usual result is that the stone yields, and yields a deeper black.

lines.zh: §8握着 {item} 的人容易相信底下有答案。§7底下通常只有更多的问题，以及一种可以熔的问题。
lines.en: §8A person holding {item} tends to believe the answer is below. §7Below there are usually more questions, and one kind that can be smelted.

lines.zh: §6{item} 的尖是一个很窄的野心。§8窄的野心最容易扎进不该扎的矿脉。
lines.en: §6The point of {item} is a very narrow ambition. §8Narrow ambitions are the easiest to drive into a vein they should not touch.

lines.zh: §d{item} 把后果装在玻璃里。§8玻璃很薄。后果不薄。
lines.en: §d{item} keeps a consequence in glass. §8The glass is thin. The consequence is not.

lines.zh: §5喝下 {item} 之前，先问它想改你的哪一条。§7血、速度，还是你还以为属于自己的那点时间。
lines.en: §5Before you drink {item}, ask which line of you it means to edit. §7The blood, the speed, or the little time you still think is yours.

lines.zh: §d{item} 的颜色是一种预告。§8预告通常比正文诚实，也比正文更难拒绝。
lines.en: §dThe color of {item} is a preview. §8Previews are usually more honest than the text, and harder to refuse.

lines.zh: §c{item} 把距离缩短成臂长。§8臂长是一种很亲密的判决。
lines.en: §c{item} shortens distance to the length of an arm. §8An arm's length is a very intimate verdict.

lines.zh: §7{item} 不出鞘的时候，只是一种沉重的暗示。§8暗示如果足够沉，就不需要说完。
lines.en: §7While {item} stays sheathed, it is only a heavy implication. §8If the implication is heavy enough, it does not need to be finished.

lines.zh: §7{item} 是一只被允许延长的手。§8延长的手能干更多活，也能犯更远的错。
lines.en: §7{item} is a hand that has been permitted to grow longer. §8A longer hand can do more work, and make a more distant mistake.

lines.zh: §8你靠 {item} 跟世界谈判。§7世界通常只同意被敲开，不同意被说服。
lines.en: §8You negotiate with the world through {item}. §7The world usually agrees to be opened. It does not agree to be persuaded.

lines.zh: §6{item} 会钝。§8钝是工具在提醒你：连它都要休息，你凭什么一直锋利。
lines.en: §6{item} will go dull. §8Dullness is the tool reminding you that even it must rest, so why should you stay sharp forever.
